description: Deferred review items tracked across all phases. Each entry maps to a source review comment that was deemed reasonable but deferred to a later phase. Check this file at each phase integration gate to identify items that may have been resolved as a side effect of other work.

items.item: assertInside does not guard against symlink escape
items.detail: resolve() only handles literal '..' text traversal; a symlink inside the sandbox that points outside can be followed to escape the root, breaking R7 (file operations confined to the sandbox dir). Acceptable in Phase 0 as a local Mock, not a security boundary. Fix: validate the real path with realpathSync/fstat before allowing the operation.
items.notes: Resolved in task 1.4: shared path-guard.ts assertInside now canonicalizes root and target (nearest existing ancestor fallback for writes) with realpathSync, rejecting any symlink that redirects outside the root, plus dangling symlinks (target nonexistent) rejected via lstat during the walk-up — writes through a dangling escaping symlink are blocked. Used by both LocalTempSandbox and DockerSandbox. Covered by packages/runtime/sandbox/test/path-guard.test.ts (symlink read-escape, symlinked-parent write-escape, in-root symlink allowed, dangling final symlink, dangling symlinked parent). [2026-08-27 PR#17 review] TOCTOU between assertInside and the fs call remains (DEF-004), out of scope here.

items.item: teardown/write use hand-written dirnameOf/basenameOf string splitting
items.detail: Replace the hand-written dirnameOf/basenameOf string-splitting helpers with node:path dirname/basename for robustness and to avoid fragile edge cases.
items.notes: Resolved in task 1.4: local-temp-sandbox.ts teardown/write now use node:path dirname/basename; the hand-written helpers were removed.

items.item: Architecture doc §3 tools subdirectory naming (fs-server wording) inconsistent with implementation
items.detail: Implementation follows the AGENTS.md naming {fs,test,git,lint,sandbox} (user-decided); the architecture doc §3 originally used an fs-server wording. Migrated from the legacy embedded [DEF] in task 0.1 notes. Verified resolved during /pr-review-agora step 7: 系统架构设计文档.md no longer contains any fs-server wording (§3 is now a generic tools/ note).
items.notes: Legacy entry migrated per standing decision DEF (task notes keep only a ledger pointer).

items.item: TOCTOU symlink race (CWE-367) between path validation and fs operation
items.detail: WorktreeFsService performs a synchronous lexical path validation then a separate fs call; a concurrent process replacing the target/an ancestor with an escaping symlink between assertInside and readFileSync/writeFileSync can break R7 confinement. Definitive fix needs openat-under-trusted-fd or an isolated concurrently-writable worktree; Node 20 lacks a clean dir-relative open API and the change is too large for the PR scope.
items.notes: packages/tools/fs/src/fs-service.ts + worktree-registry.ts, plus the sandbox read/write path (LocalTempSandbox/DockerSandbox host-side read/write validate via assertInside then perform the fs call). Release condition: DockerSandbox (1.4) provides worktree isolation as mitigation; re-evaluate whether an openat refactor is needed when true parallelism lands (Phase 4 / 9.2). [2026-08-27] Mitigation landed in task 1.4: DockerSandbox confines run() to a per-task container (NetworkMode none, bind-mounted worktree root), so the concurrently-writable host dir is no longer the command execution boundary; sandbox read/write TOCTOU remains open for LocalTempSandbox-hosted fs operations, tracked here until Phase 4 re-evaluation. [2026-08-27 PR#17 review] CodeRabbit raised the same TOCTOU on the sandbox read/write path (local-temp-sandbox.ts:44); acknowledged, covered by this entry (definitive fix needs descriptor-relative no-follow ops or an isolated worktree — out of PR scope, deferred to Phase 4). [2026-08-31 Phase 4 exit re-evaluation, Leader approved] Phase 4 still uses the sequential WorkerRuntime fallback, so the true concurrent replacement window has not expanded beyond the known host-side risk. Keep the item open and retarget it to Phase 9, where bounded parallel workers and worktree integration create the intended re-evaluation point.

items.item: lint MCP server not implemented in Phase 1
items.detail: Phase 1 tool servers cover fs (1.1), test (1.2), git (1.3); packages/tools/lint is an empty stub and no lint server task exists in Phase 1. The §2 permission matrix declares lint for CODER/REVIEWER; the tool loader (task 1.5) must keep the RoleSpec.tools 'lint' entry resolvable-but-unavailable (skipped at registration), and Phase 1 exit tests must not require lint.
items.notes: User-approved deferral during task 1.5 planning ([2026-08-27]). RESOLVED in task 2.5 (user directed in-PR resolution): packages/tools/lint implements the §6 lint-server (`check(worktree, paths) -> issues[]`) as a Biome wrapper — WorktreeLintService spawns `node <biome-bin> lint <paths> --reporter=json` with cwd=the registered worktree root (no shell, worktree-relative path validation, registry allowlist hardening mirrored from fs/test services), parses the JSON diagnostics into {file,line,message,rule,severity}; bridge grants logical `lint` → lint_check (wire-safe) and CODER/REVIEWER's matrix `lint` entries now resolve for real. Verified: 12 unit/round-trip tests over the real biome binary (packages/tools/lint/test) + REVIEWER exercises lint_check in-loop in the phase2-exit six-role chains (lint-clean math.js → []).

items.item: TESTER git capability granularity: main-repo mutations vs worktree-scoped reads
items.detail: CodeRabbit flagged that TESTER (RoleSpec.tools includes 'git') is granted the full git group via LOGICAL_GROUPS — git_createWorktree + git_applyPatch + git_diff + git_merge — including main-repo mutations (createWorktree, merge) that go beyond the §2 matrix's 'git(worktree)' qualifier (worktree-scoped ops). The implementation is faithful to the matrix (TESTER git(worktree)=✓, full grant), so this is a spec-granularity decision, not a code bug: the bridge's single 'git' logical group cannot express read-only variants (ARCH=只读, REVIEWER=只读 diff are unrepresentable). Also resolved in PR #18 for Phase 0 by the PHASE0_TOOL_SURFACE gate (spec §9 '工具只接 fs + sandbox.run' — git phase-gated out of the Phase 0 runtime), so the over-grant only matters once git is exercised in Phase 1+. Resolution: split LOGICAL_GROUPS into worktree-scoped (git.applyPatch/git.diff) vs main-repo (git.createWorktree/git.merge) groups, or add 'git.readonly'→git.diff, per a human spec ruling on TESTER/ARCH/REVIEWER grants when the Phase 1 composition root lands.
items.notes: Deferred in /pr-review-agora for PR #18: requires a human spec decision on the §2 matrix granularity (does TESTER's git(worktree)=✓ include main-repo merge/createWorktree?). RESOLVED in task 2.5 (user-approved): LOGICAL_GROUPS `git` redefined as worktree-scoped (git.applyPatch + git.diff, matching the matrix's `git(worktree)` qualifier) + new `git.readonly` (git.diff only) for ARCHITECT/REVIEWER; git_createWorktree/git_merge granted to NO model role (composition-root/integrate-node ops). RoleSpec change limited to roles-definitions (ARCH/REVIEWER `git`→`git.readonly`); PHASE0_ROSTER untouched (R9). Documented in 详细设计 §2 [2026-08-28 实装记录]; verified by phase2-exit DEF-006 chain + phase1-exit direct git chain (real binary, full createWorktree→applyPatch→diff→merge).

items.item: Review-pass convergence lacks leader confirmation in Phase 2 (humanGate lands in Phase 8)
items.detail: 详细设计 §3 convergence rule reads 'test 全过 + review 通过(经 leader 确认)', but humanGate (leader arbitration surface) is a Phase 8 deliverable. User ruled during task 2.2 planning ([2026-08-28]): Phase 2 simplifies convergence to 'REVIEWER pass → finalize' with no leader confirmation step; R3 (leader sole authority) is not violated because no agent auto-consensus replaces a leader ruling — the confirmation semantics simply do not exist yet.
items.notes: Resolution condition: when humanGate lands in Phase 8, wire REVIEWER-pass convergence through a leader confirmation gate (blocking humanGate per D4 terminate-and-fork) instead of finalizing directly. [2026-08-28 task 2.5] Phase 2 exit tests assert the ruled simplification end-to-end: REVIEWER-approved verdicts finalize directly with humanGate unset (phase2-exit chains 1-3, DEF-007 noted in the review-loop block). Check this entry at the Phase 8 exit gate. [2026-09-05 Leader approved spec disposition] D16 now defines the closure: REVIEWER approved only creates a completion candidate; task 8.5 must implement a review-bound completion_confirmation D4 gate, canonical Leader completion Decision, approve→finalize and request_changes→CODER resume paths. [2026-09-05 task 8.5 resolved] Coordinator now opens the review-bound completion gate; the D9 resolver atomically records the canonical Leader Message, Decision and receipt; true Fork resume cross-validates those facts before approve→finalize or request_changes→CODER. Evidence: phase8-exit real chain plus completion domain/coordinator/message-flow regressions and cumulative Phase 5 Docker chains.

items.item: Bind routing roster and WorkerRuntime roster into one source (composition-root ergonomics)
items.detail: CodeRabbit flagged that OrchestrationDeps.roster (routing) is independent from WorkerRuntimeDeps.roster (execution): a caller mismatching them makes decide() route PM/ARCHITECT/REVIEWER to a runtime whose specOf() throws UnknownRoleError. Verified in /pr-review-agora: the failure mode is a loud explicit UnknownRoleError (fail-fast, not silent corruption), and all current call sites (orchestrator.test orchestrationWith, lru-cache e2e, phase0-exit, phase1-exit ×2) pass PHASE0_ROSTER to both consistently. The task-2.2 user-approved plan explicitly chose 'OrchestrationDeps += roster? forwarded to decide()', so re-binding via a WorkerRuntime roster getter changes an approved interface design and needs a human ruling.
items.notes: Resolution condition: when the full 6-role composition root lands (DEFAULT_ROSTER first used outside unit tests), either expose the roster on WorkerRuntime and derive routing from it (drop OrchestrationDeps.roster), or validate roster coverage at the composition root. RESOLVED in task 2.5 (user-approved, option b): phase2-runtime shares ONE DEFAULT_ROSTER constant for routing + execution and enforces assertRosterBinding (coverage equality) at assembly; WorkerRuntime gained a read-only `roster` getter for the check. OrchestrationDeps/DecideOptions interfaces untouched (task 2.2 approved design stands); option (a) interface consolidation stays available if Phase 3 composition work reopens it. Verified by phase2-exit DEF-008 chain (pass on shared binding, throws on mismatch mentioning the missing role).

items.item: Idempotent re-escalation guard for resumed capped states (no duplicate escalation messages)
items.detail: CodeRabbit's merge-risk note: re-running a capped state (e.g. after a leader ruling that clears humanGate but not iterationCount) appends a second escalation message, because escalationMessage() mints a fresh msgId and deduplicatedAppend only dedups identical msgIds. Verified in /pr-review-agora: within a single runOrchestration the human_gate route halts immediately (exactly one escalation per run), and no current call site re-runs a capped state, so nothing duplicates today. The real exposure arrives in Phase 8, where humanGate switches to D4 terminate-and-fork and resumed states become routine.
items.notes: Resolution condition: when the Phase 8 humanGate body (terminate-and-fork per D4) lands, ensure state re-entry is idempotent end-to-end — either guard ifIterationLimit on 'humanGate already set with the same reason' or rebuild the escalation from the safePoint event cursor instead of re-appending. Check this entry when task 8.x humanGate implementation starts. [2026-09-05 spec review] Static inspection indicates the iteration_limit resolver now atomically resets iterationCount to 0 and persisted gate/receipt facts prevent capped-state re-entry, so the original exposure is likely removed. [2026-09-05 task 8.5 resolved] The iteration_limit resolver resets iterationCount to 0 in the same commit that records its receipt and clears the gate. Same-action replay reuses the canonical receipt and does not append another escalation or gate. Evidence: phase8-exit replay case and phase8/iteration-limit-replay deterministic Eval.

items.item: AppState.pendingPatch has no write op in the §1 Mutation union
items.detail: §1 defines pendingPatch (code-layer reference field) but the Mutation union lists no op for it — same gap class as #22/#25. Task 2.4 projection reads it read-only with an explicit null default (R9, no silent absence). Unlocked writers are consumer-driven per repo precedent (2.2 requirements, 2.4 conventions), and there is no real consumer yet: TESTER/REVIEWER consume worktree path refs via branchOrPatch.worktrees and can pull diffs themselves with git/fs tools (iron rule 2 — truth lives in the worktree).
items.notes: Resolution condition: unlock the pendingPatch set op when a real consumer lands — evaluate at task 2.5 e2e (does the CODER patch-submission flow need to carry patch metadata through State for the REVIEWER pendingDiff slice?), else slide to Phase 3 patch-reference work. EVALUATED at 2.5 (user-approved disposition): the six-role e2e proves the CODER→REVIEWER patch flow works entirely via worktree refs (branchOrPatch.worktrees slice) + REVIEWER's in-loop git_diff — final state has pendingPatch unset for the whole run (asserted in phase2-exit chain 1), so no consumer exists. Sliding to Phase 3 patch-reference work; unlock still follows the pre-paved path (SET_FIELDS + ENABLED_SET_FIELDS + applySet case, signature unchanged) plus an R12 实装记录 in 详细设计方案 §1. [2026-08-30 user ruling, option A] Phase 3 is closing with no consumer landed, so the entry is re-pointed target_phase 3 → 4 instead of lingering past its target: the pendingPatch write op stays locked until a real patch-reference consumer appears (unlock path unchanged). Re-check at the Phase 4 exit gate. [2026-08-31 Phase 4 exit re-evaluation, Leader approved] Repository-wide inspection still finds only read-side projection plus fixture coverage; the real CODER→REVIEWER chain continues to use worktree references and git_diff, with no pendingPatch writer or consumer. Keep the Mutation op locked and retarget the next review to Phase 9 worktree integration.

items.item: Write-side legality of cross-topic supersedes (assertSupersedesIsLegal does not check topic equality)
items.detail: CodeRabbit flagged that a decision on topic Y may legally supersede a decision on topic X: assertSupersedesIsLegal (core/domain/ledger.ts:58-71) only validates target existence + agent-cannot-supersede-leader, and addDecision's conflict signal filters same-topic entries, so a cross-topic supersedes is constructible through the public API. Read-side impact is already fixed in PR #31 (collapseSupersededDecisions now collapses only in-topic pointers; cross-topic targets keep full fidelity, so projections never hide a topic's only decision text). The write-side question — should cross-topic supersedes be rejected at the ledger boundary — is a new L1 domain rule not defined by spec §1 (which only mandates target-existence + authority checks and explicitly parks conflict-classification logic in Phase 8), so adding it requires a spec ruling per R12, not a silent code change.
items.notes: Resolution condition: when Phase 8 conflict classification lands (spec §1 '同 topic 冲突以原始信号返回，分类逻辑留 Phase 8'), rule whether supersedes must be same-topic and, if so, extend assertSupersedesIsLegal with a topic-equality check + ledger regression tests + an R12 实装记录 in 详细设计方案 §1. Until then the read-side collapse is topic-scoped, which bounds the blast radius to reduced compression (never information loss). [2026-09-05 Leader approved ruling] supersedes must reference a current Decision with the same topic; cross-topic writes fail-fast. D14 decision-target resolutions already inherit the target topic. [2026-09-05 task 8.5 resolved] assertSupersedesIsLegal now rejects both non-current and cross-topic targets at the L1/reducer boundary; legacy Phase 3 fixtures no longer construct an illegal edge. Ledger and reducer regressions cover both failures.

items.source: /test-phase-agora Phase 3 exit coverage review + user ruling (2026-08-30)
items.item: Coordinator does not generate handoffPackets at role switches (five nextRole flips in coordinator.ts)
items.detail: Spec source: 开发计划安排 §6.3 交接包「生成逻辑：在角色切换时由 Coordinator 触发」(mirrored by task 3.2's own description). Task 3.2 遗留① deferred the wiring to 3.3/3.5 (resolution condition: the five nextRole flips in coordinator.ts dispatch/evaluate functions), but 3.3 (projection scope) and 3.5 (user-approved scope: barrel export + exit test only) both shipped without it, and the deferral was never ledgered. Surfaced by the Phase 3 exit coverage review (/test-phase-agora): cross-package chain coverage 5/6 — phase3-exit seeds handoff packets manually, so a real run has no generation path. Already in place: HandoffPacket structure + assertValidHandoff/assertAppendableHandoff gates (core/domain/handoff.ts), the reducer append gate with keyDecisions referential integrity, and R1 seam assertions in phase3-exit — only the generation trigger is missing.
items.notes: Resolved in task 4.4: Coordinator now uses a single post-decision attachCoordinationArtifacts seam to append a HandoffPacket whenever an existing worker nextRole changes to a different worker role. The implementation is generic rather than limited to the original five flips; it derives leader decision ids and structured failure fileRefs/openIssues from State and still passes the reducer shape/referential-integrity gate. Evidence: packages/core/orchestration/test/coordinator.test.ts covers generic generation and non-generation cases; tests/integration/phase2/phase2-exit.test.ts runs the real Harness/MCP/LocalTempSandbox chain through PM→ARCHITECT→CODER→TESTER→REVIEWER and asserts four generated packets without manual seeding; tests/integration/cross-phase/phase4-coordination-ledger.test.ts verifies deterministic cross-package persistence/projection.

items.source: task 4.2 plan ruling ③ (user-delegated execution, PR human review pending as merge backstop)
items.item: Review rework granularity under multi-subtask Tier 2 (reopen-all is a conservative superset)
items.detail: Task 4.2 ruling ③: with multiple subtasks, REVIEWER changes_requested reopens ALL subtasks and re-activates the first in array order — a conservative superset that never misses feedback targeting an earlier subtask, but may re-run unaffected units. Phase 4 has no per-subtask review refs (reviewComments are Record<string,unknown> from a thin executor), so narrower targeting is not yet implementable without inventing schema.
items.notes: Resolution condition: when Phase 9 parallel dispatch lands, carry subtask refs in reviewComments (REVIEWER sees per-subtask worktree refs via branchOrPatch) and narrow reopenForRework to the referenced subset, keeping reopen-all as the fallback when no refs are present. Check this entry at the Phase 9 exit gate.

items.item: Phase 5 Task State JSON persistence is specified but not yet implemented
items.detail: Task 5.3 implemented the D6/D7 Phase 5 boundary: zero-dependency JSON task snapshots, atomic replacement, commit-before-delivery, idempotent msgId handling, and refresh/process-restart recovery. SQLite remains an optional future adapter.
items.notes: Resolved 2026-08-31 by task 5.3. JsonTaskStateStore tests cover create-if-absent, atomic snapshots, per-task serialized concurrent commits, idempotent replay, path confinement, and corrupt JSON. MessageService tests prove commit-before-publish and no rollback on delivery failure. Web tests and production-browser G5 prove payload-free SSE, refresh recovery, and recovery after stopping/restarting Next from .data/projects/{projectId}/tasks/{taskId}/state.json.

items.item: SSE and HTTP routes do not validate canonical Channel scope; worker inbox lacks participant isolation
items.detail: Task 5.3 requires projectId/taskId/channelId scope and server-stamps browser messages as leader, so caller-provided role spoofing is closed. The remaining Phase 6 gap is canonical Channel integrity: routes do not reject unknown, cross-task, or closed channels before State commit, and worker inbox routing does not yet filter by Project.channels participants. Browser account authentication remains explicitly out of scope: within the trusted single-user boundary the browser is leader, and leader is a participant of every Channel. Resolving this item therefore does not make unauthenticated public deployment safe.
items.notes: Task 5.3 completed the Phase 5 portion: HTTP/SSE use projectId/taskId/channelId and browser POST identity is server-owned leader, with a negative spoofing test. [2026-09-01 Leader-approved spec review] Resolution condition is now precise and testable: persist canonical Project.channels, reject unknown/cross-task/closed channels before State commit, prove non-participant workers cannot read or publish to a sub channel, and prove rejected publication neither mutates AppState.messages nor emits MessageCommitted. GET/POST browser tests operate as the server-derived leader, who may access every Channel by invariant; they test invalid Channel scope rather than fabricate an unauthenticated non-leader identity. [2026-09-01 Task 6.1 resolved] JsonProjectChannelStore persists canonical Project.channels with restart recovery; MessageService and HTTP/SSE reject invalid scope before commit; DerivedChannelInbox enforces participant visibility; negative tests prove no State or MessageCommitted/SSE side effect. This resolves DEF-015 under its Leader-approved Channel-integrity scope. Full account authentication remains an explicit deployment non-goal under D8, so the trusted single-user boundary is unchanged and resolution must not be represented as public multi-user safety.

items.item: Generic autonomous Coordinator routing for arbitrary custom roles
items.detail: The prior blueprint claimed that adding any RoleSpec required no orchestration change, but the production Coordinator has a deliberate six-role state machine and routeWhen only evaluates a small predicate vocabulary. It does not define ordering when several custom roles match, the mutations/output contract a custom role must produce, or failure fallback. Phase 7 therefore guarantees persistent custom-role registration, projection/tool scoping, and explicit Leader @ROLE dispatch through the generic worker, but does not claim arbitrary-role autonomous routing.
items.notes: Resolution condition: define a versioned generic routing contract covering candidate priority/tie-breaking, accepted routeWhen predicates or another deterministic selector, per-role output/mutation schema, authorization, failure fallback, iteration accounting, and humanGate escalation; then add deterministic and real-chain tests showing a custom role enters and exits the topology without hard-coded role branches. Reassess in Phase 10 after the default six-role product flow and external executor boundary are stable.
